key_insight: This paper shows that large language models can do more than generate text—they can help design better optimization algorithms. The key idea is to build a verified problem contract and then evolve a set of complementary heuristics that work together when no single solver is enough.
problem_solved: Combinatorial optimization often requires hand-crafted heuristics, and a single algorithm usually performs well only on a subset of problem types. The paper addresses the challenge of automatically creating robust optimization methods that can handle diverse and difficult instances.
method: Create a verified problem contract that precisely defines the optimization task and constraints.
Use an LLM-based framework called LACE to generate and refine candidate heuristics.
Evolve a portfolio of complementary heuristics so different methods can cover each other's weaknesses.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a scalable way to automate algorithm design rather than relying solely on manual heuristic engineering. It could improve solver robustness and make optimization systems more adaptable across problem settings.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: problem contract -> heuristic generation -> portfolio evolution -> final solver

paper_title: Large language models discover complementary heuristics for combinatorial optimization
paper_authors: Huatian Gong, Shuaian Wang, Dongping Song, Jiuh-Biing Sheu, Ran Yan
